title: Foundation of Innovation Workshop (16–18 February 2026) Organized under the aegis of the Career Development Centre.
excerpt: INTRODUCTION A three-day workshop titled “Foundation of Innovation” was organized from 16 to 18 February 2026 under the aegis of […]
content:
INTRODUCTION
A three-day workshop titled “Foundation of Innovation” was organized from 16 to 18 February 2026 under the aegis of the Career Development Centre. The workshop aimed
to develop entrepreneurial thinking, innovation capabilities, and problem-solving skills among participants. Through expert sessions, discussions, and practical activities,
participants were introduced to the fundamentals of entrepreneurship, innovation
processes, design thinking, and business model development. The workshop emphasized transforming ideas into practical solutions that create both social and economic value.

Day 1: Entrepreneurial Mindset, Innovation, and Opportunity Recognition
The first day of the workshop focused on developing the entrepreneurial mindset and understanding the innovation process.
The keynote session “Entrepreneur DNA & Mindset Development” was delivered by Dr.Rajbir Singh. The session emphasized that entrepreneurship begins with clarity of purpose, discipline, and persistence in execution, rather than simply having a unique idea.
Participants were introduced to the LUV Test (Large, Urgent, Valuable) for evaluating business ideas and were guided through the entrepreneurial journey from idea generation to feasibility, prototyping, launching, and scaling.
The second session, “Implementing Ideas: From Innovation to Impact,” was conducted by Prof. Ravinder Kaur. The session discussed different forms of innovation such as incremental, architectural, disruptive, and radical innovation, and highlighted that innovation is a continuous and iterative process involving idea generation, testing, and improvement. Real-life examples were discussed to demonstrate how everyday problems can inspire meaningful innovations.
The third session, “Opportunity Recognition – From Idea to Impact,” was conducted by Gourav Aggarwal. The session explained how entrepreneurial opportunities emerge at the intersection of problems, capabilities, and timing. Participants engaged in discussions and activities to identify real-world problems and convert them into opportunity statements that could potentially lead to viable entrepreneurial ventures.

Day 2: Empathy, User Research, and Ideation
The second day of the workshop emphasized user-centered thinking and research methods in entrepreneurship.
The first session was conducted by Prof. Ravinder Kaur, who discussed the importance of understanding users and identifying their real needs before developing solutions. The session highlighted how entrepreneurs must carefully analyze user behavior, preferences, and challenges to design effective innovations.
The second session, “Empathy in Business and Entrepreneurship,” was conducted by Mr.Shubham Chavriya. The session explained empathy as a strategic advantage in entrepreneurship. Participants learned about the three layers of empathy—cognitive, emotional, and compassionate empathy, which help entrepreneurs understand customer perspectives and develop meaningful solutions. Practical tools such as empathy mapping, persona development, and consumer journey mapping were introduced to analyze customer needs, experiences, and emotional responses throughout their interaction with a product or service.
The third session, “Survey, Ideation, and Observation,” was conducted by Dr. Naveen Rampal. The session focused on the discovery phase of innovation, where entrepreneurs gather insights about users through research techniques such as questionnaires, interviews, observation, and secondary data analysis. Participants were also introduced to ideation techniques, including brainstorming, reverse brainstorming, affinity mapping, and lateral thinking, followed by evaluating alternatives based on feasibility, impact, cost, and practicality.

Day 3: Design Thinking, Business Models, and Pitching
The final day of the workshop focused on applying innovation frameworks to develop practical business solutions.
The first session, “Design Thinking: Principles and Process,” was conducted by Prof.Ravinder Kaur. The session introduced participants to Design Thinking as a humancentred
approach to innovation. Participants learned about the five stages of Design ,Thinking, Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test, and how this framework helps entrepreneurs create user-focused solutions.
The second session was conducted by Gourav Aggarwal, who introduced participants to Business Model Canvas Mapping. The session explained the nine components of the Business Model Canvas, including customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships, and cost structure. Participants learned how these components help transform innovative ideas into structured and viable business models.

Conclusion
The “Foundation of Innovation” workshop successfully provided participants with valuable exposure to the principles of entrepreneurship, innovation, and design thinking.
Through expert-led sessions, practical frameworks, and interactive activities, participants gained insights into identifying problems, developing innovative solutions, and structuring sustainable business models.
Overall, the workshop helped participants develop creative thinking, empathy-driven innovation, and structured problem-solving skills, which are essential for entrepreneurial success and meaningful societal impact.
Report Prepared By:
Shubham Chavriya
Convener, Career Development Centre
Delhi College of Arts and Commerce
University of Delhi

title: Samarth Bharat Vichar Goshti 2026
excerpt: Date: 15 January 2026Venue: NDMC Convention Centre, Sansad Marg, New DelhiTheme: “Skilled Youth for a Capable India; Capable Youth for […]
content:
Date: 15 January 2026
Venue: NDMC Convention Centre, Sansad Marg, New Delhi
Theme: “Skilled Youth for a Capable India; Capable Youth for a Developed India”

On 15 January 2026, Samarth Bharat successfully organized the Samarth Bharat Seminar 2026 at the prestigious NDMC Convention Centre, Sansad Marg, New Delhi, bringing together distinguished leaders, industry experts, policymakers, educators, and aspiring youth under the inspiring theme, “Skilled Youth for a Capable India; Capable Youth for a Developed India.” The seminar served as a powerful platform to promote the vision of a skilled, self-reliant, and empowered nation by emphasizing the transformative role of vocational education, entrepreneurship, and youth development in nation-building.

The event was honoured by the gracious presence of Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Delhi, who attended as the Chief Guest. In her inspiring address, she highlighted that skill development is the strongest foundation for employment, dignity, and self-reliance. She encouraged young people to embrace discipline, continuous learning, and self-confidence while preparing themselves to contribute meaningfully to the nation’s progress. Her motivating message reinforced the importance of equipping India’s youth with practical skills and a positive mindset to build a prosperous and developed nation.

The seminar’s keynote address was delivered by Dr. Krishna Gopal, Joint General Secretary (Sah-Sarkaryavah), Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). He emphasized that skill development extends far beyond employment, describing it as a powerful tool for character building, service to society, personal growth, and national development. He encouraged young people to combine professional excellence with strong values, discipline, and a commitment to social responsibility, inspiring them to become responsible citizens who contribute to the country’s long-term progress.

The event was presided over by Shri Motilal Oswal, Co-founder and Chairman of Motilal Oswal Financial Services, who shared valuable insights on entrepreneurship, financial discipline, and long-term career planning. Addressing the youth, he emphasized the importance of setting clear goals, adopting an entrepreneurial mindset, and making informed financial decisions. He encouraged participants to transform opportunities into achievements through determination, innovation, and strategic planning, reminding them that success is built upon consistent effort and the right guidance.

The seminar was further enriched by the esteemed presence of Shri Nandkishore Agarwal, Chairman of Crystal Group, and Shri Om Prakash Goyal, President of Bhaurao Deoras Seva Nyas. Their participation added immense value to the event, reflecting a shared commitment towards youth empowerment, social development, and strengthening India’s skill ecosystem through collaborative efforts.

Throughout the seminar, engaging discussions highlighted the growing importance of skill development, vocational education, entrepreneurship, leadership, financial literacy, and industry readiness in preparing India’s youth for the future. The event inspired students, educators, professionals, entrepreneurs, and social leaders to actively participate in the nation’s journey toward becoming a globally competitive and self-reliant economy. It reinforced the belief that investing in skills not only creates employment opportunities but also builds confident individuals capable of driving sustainable national growth.

The Samarth Bharat Seminar 2026 also received extensive media coverage from leading national and regional media organizations, including DD News, The Times of India, Punjab News Express, New Kerala, Global Governance News, India Mastermind, and several other prominent print and digital publications. The widespread recognition highlighted the seminar’s significance and amplified Samarth Bharat’s ongoing efforts to promote skill development, employment generation, and youth empowerment across the country.

The successful organization of this seminar further strengthens Samarth Bharat’s unwavering commitment to building a Skilled, Self-Reliant, and Empowered India. By fostering collaboration between government, industry, educational institutions, and society, Samarth Bharat continues to create meaningful opportunities that enable young people to develop industry-relevant skills, embrace innovation, and become confident contributors to the nation’s growth.

Together, we are shaping a future where every skilled youth becomes a catalyst for a stronger, self-reliant, and developed India.

title: DSEU Signs MoU with Samarth Bharat and Sewa Bharti to Promote Skill Development and SocialUpliftment
excerpt: New Delhi, October 17, 2025: Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University (DSEU) signed Memorandums ofUnderstanding (MoUs) with Samarth Bharat and Sewa […]
content:
New Delhi, October 17, 2025: Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University (DSEU) signed Memorandums of
Understanding (MoUs) with Samarth Bharat and Sewa Bharti on 17 October 2025, to collaboratively strengthen skill development, social empowerment, and community engagement initiatives in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

The ceremony began with a warm welcome address by Dr. Pankaj Lathar, Joint Director (Public Relations) and Campus Director, DSEU Dwarka, who extended greetings to all dignitaries and partners present, including Dr. Shonal Gupta (Coordinator), Sh. Nikhil Bansal (Patron), Sh. Rakesh Kumar Gupta (Co-coordinator), Prof. Ravinder Kaur (Co-coordinator, CDC), among others, from Samarth Bharat. Also in attendance were representatives from Seva Bharti, including Sh. Sushil Gupta (General Secretary), Sh. Gulshan Narang (Secretary), Sh. Amarnath (Community Reach), among others. From DSEU, the gathering was graced by the presence of the Hon’ble Vice Chancellor, Prof. (Dr.) Ashok Kumar Nagawat, Registrar, Prof. Gagan Dhawan, Director (Academics), Prof. Kamna Sachdeva, Joint Director (Partnerships), Dr. Suman Dhawan, Campus Directors, and faculty members.

Speaking about Samarth Bharat, the representatives shared that their organization, an initiative of the Bhartiya Drishtikon Seva Nyas (BDSN), envisions empowering the socially and economically weaker sections of society to become self-reliant and live with dignity. Through skill development and training programs, Samarth Bharat equips unemployed youth with practical skills for employment or entrepreneurship, emphasizing nationbuilding.

Representatives from Sewa Bharti highlighted the organization’s volunteer-driven approach and its motto “Sewa Hi Paramo Dharma” — service as the highest virtue — describing their impactful work across educational, social, self-reliance projects, including disaster relief, child welfare, women empowerment, and rehabilitation of marginalized communities. They elaborated on their government-approved adoption agency, cochlear implant initiatives for hearing-impaired children, etc.

Following these addresses, Dr. Lathar invited the Joint Director (Partnerships) to commence the formal MoU signing. He also shared details of other recent partnerships DSEU has undertaken, reaffirming the university’s commitment to linking skill-based education with societal development.

In his address, Hon’ble Vice Chancellor emphasized DSEU’s vision of transforming education from a colonial model into a more practical, skill-oriented framework. He stressed that skill-based learning must reach every section of society through short-term, outcome-oriented programs — adding that “the real measure of education is not the length of the course, but the mastery of the skill.” He also highlighted that all MoUs signed by DSEU are reviewed quarterly to ensure tangible outcomes and meaningful collaboration. He expressed confidence that partnerships with Samarth Bharat and Sewa Bharti will catalyze new skill development programs, benefiting underprivileged and marginalized communities.

The event concluded with a heartfelt Vote of Thanks by Director Academics, Prof. Kamna Sachdeva, who reiterated that “skill is the foundation of development and growth.”

Dr. Pankaj Lathar
Joint Director (Public Relations)

title: Seed Fund Accelerator Pitching Competition

In pursuit of nurturing innovation and entrepreneurial spirit, the Udhmodya Committee of
Shivaji College organized the Seed Fund Accelerator Pitching Competition on September
24, 2025, at the college premises in Raja Garden, New Delhi. The event provided a vibrant
platform for budding entrepreneurs to showcase their early-stage startups, with the aim of
turning their innovative ideas into reality through expert mentorship and essential financial
support.

The competition witnessed enthusiastic participation from young innovators, whose passion and creativity created an atmosphere of dynamism and collaboration. The presence of esteemed dignitaries added immense value to the program. The college had the privilege of hosting Mr. Praveen Kapoor, a seasoned professional with over 32 years of experience in Business Growth, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation, who has mentored more than 100 incubators and facilitated over 350 corporate collaborations across India. The second guest of honor, Prof. Ravinder Kaur, MoE Innovation Ambassador, Mentor at T-Hub Hyderabad, and Executive Innovation Officer at Udhmodya Foundation, brought with her rich experience
of guiding startups to scale impactful ventures. The third distinguished guest was Mr. Shonal Gupta, a Learning and Skill Development professional with more than 30 years of experience across corporate, government, and social organizations, and currently the Project Head of Samarth Bharat, where he is empowering youth through re-skilling, innovation, and entrepreneurship initiatives.

The felicitation of dignitaries was gracefully conducted by Prof. Virendra Bhardwaj, Principal of Shivaji College, and Prof. Suman Kharbanda, Coordinator of the Incubation Centre, with bouquets presented by the Karitri Project of Enactus Shivaji. The event also acknowledged the continuous guidance and mentorship of Dr. Chhavi Sharma, Convenor of Udhmodya, whose vision and support remain the backbone of every milestone achieved by the Committee.

The core highlight of the day was the startup pitching round, where student teams presented their business models to the panel of judges. Each pitch reflected rigorous research, creativity, and problem-solving potential. After thoughtful deliberation, the winning venture was declared—Up Upasti, which secured seed funding of ₹25,000 to advance their entrepreneurial journey. Alongside, two promising startups, Capilo and Green Energy Ko, were extended valuable support in the form of mentorship, access to labs, and other resources, ensuring that their innovative ideas continue to grow and make impact.

The competition reinforced the belief that in entrepreneurship, there are no losses, only learning opportunities. The judges inspired participants to see this platform as the beginning of many more chances to refine and scale their ideas. The event concluded with palpable excitement and motivation among students, as they left with not only encouragement but also a stronger resolve to pursue their entrepreneurial ambitions.

By providing students with such platforms, the Udhmodya Committee once again reaffirmed its mission of cultivating entrepreneurial confidence, resilience, and innovation-driven thinking, truly transforming dreams into ventures and passion into purpose.

title: My Career, My Choice – A Step Towards Clarity in Career Building
excerpt: The Career Development Cell (Samarth Bharat), under the Innovation and Incubation Cell (Udhmodya Foundation) of Mata Sundri College for Women, […]
content:
The Career Development Cell (Samarth Bharat), under the Innovation and Incubation Cell (Udhmodya Foundation) of Mata Sundri College for Women, organised an insightful workshop on “My Career, My Choice” on 17th September 2025 at Bebe Nanki Hall. The session was graced by the guest speaker Mr. Shonal Gupta, Convenor – Samarth Bharat, and witnessed the participation of over 80+ enthusiastic students from across courses and years.

The workshop began with an interactive activity, where students were invited to share their career status through two engaging boards – “Career Wall” and “Still Exploring.” On colourful bookmarks, they noted whether they had already decided on their career paths or were still exploring, and placed them on the respective charts. This activity not only broke the ice but also set the tone for a reflective and thought-provoking session.

Mr. Gupta highlighted how career decisions are influenced by multiple factors – environmental (family, economy), individual (skills, influence, guidance), social (norms, inequalities), and government-related (policies, infrastructure gaps). He emphasised the importance of starting early, making conscious efforts towards one’s aspirations, and surrounding oneself with mentors and peers who encourage growth rather than misguide.

He also discussed challenges like regional disparities, lack of guidance, misinformation on social media, limited exposure, and distractions that hinder career advancement. Students were encouraged to ask themselves meaningful questions such as:

  • What are my strengths and passions?
  • What do I enjoy doing in my free time?
  • What does success mean to me – only money or also satisfaction and balance?
  • Have I explored all my options?
  • What are the long-term prospects of my chosen field?

Practical solutions like internships, skill development, mapping personal strengths, and eliminating weaker career options were suggested as ways to bring clarity. Mr. Gupta also shed light on the Samarth Bharat initiatives offering training in technology, AI, Excel, Python, startups, and skill-based courses – equipping students for real-world opportunities.

The session ended with a strong message – start today, take ownership of your choices, and build the future you aspire to.

Vote of Thanks

We extend our heartfelt gratitude to our Principal, Professor Harpreet Kaur, for her constant encouragement and support in making this event possible. A special thanks to our guest speaker, Mr. Shonal Gupta, for delivering such an engaging and insightful session.

We also thank our distinguished guests, Prof. T.G. Rupa (Convener, CDC Lady Irwin College) and Dr. Karan Sachdeva (Co-Convener, CDC Lady Irwin College), for their gracious presence. Our sincere appreciation goes to our conveners, Dr. Harshmeeta Kaur Soni (convener) and Dr. Ashema Hasti(Co-convener) , for their guidance throughout.

A big round of thanks to the MSIIC team – especially Lipika Yadav (President) and Divleen Kaur (Vice-President) – for their seamless organisation and smooth management of the event. Finally, applause goes to all the students who participated wholeheartedly, making this session lively and impactful.

The workshop truly left students with not just answers but also the right questions to ask on their journey ahead – making it a transformative learning experience.

title: Nari Shakti March  – A Protest for Justice and Solidarity,Mandi House
excerpt: Date: 16th July 2024| Location: Mandi House, New Delhi  The Nari Shakti Foundation organized a powerful and peaceful protest march […]
content:
Date: 16th July 2024| Location: Mandi House, New Delhi

 The Nari Shakti Foundation organized a powerful and peaceful protest march titled Nari Shakti March in New Delhi. The march was held in strong condemnation of the ongoing violence, sexual assaults, kidnappings, and systemic oppression against Hindu women in Bangladesh, and to raise awareness about the targeted persecution of Hindus in the region.

The event served as a call to action against gender-based violence and communal atrocities, standing in solidarity with the affected women and communities across borders.

Participation by Samarth Bharat

As a strong supporter of women’s empowerment and human rights, Samarth Bharat actively participated in the march. The organization mobilized:

  • 150 trainees from 8 different skill development centers
  • 8 trainers, each representing their respective training center
  • Several senior members and volunteers of Samarth Bharat

The participants marched with banners, posters, and placards demanding justice, protection of minority rights, and international attention to the plight of Hindu women in Bangladesh. Their presence represented the voice of empowered Indian women standing in unity for their sisters beyond borders.

Highlights of the Event

  • Chants of unity and justice filled the air as participants peacefully walked from their assembly point to Mandi House, one of Delhi’s key public demonstration areas.
  • Slogans and messages emphasized “Stop atrocities on Hindu women”, “Justice for victims in Bangladesh”, and “Women’s safety is a human right”.
  • Nari Shakti Foundation leaders addressed the gathering, calling upon national and international bodies to take strong action and ensure human rights for minority women.

The march was not just a protest but also a symbol of cross-border solidarity, driven by organizations that believe in empowering women not only with skills but also with voice and dignity.

The participation of young women from Samarth Bharat training centers reflected the organization’s commitment to nurturing socially aware and responsible citizens, who are willing to stand up for justice and collective humanity.

title: Startup Accelerator Program at Delhi University

content:
Date: 27–28 October 2023
Location: Delhi University, in collaboration with Udhmodya Foundation

Under the aegis of Samarth Bharat’s Career Development Center (CDC), a two-day Startup Accelerator Program was organized at Delhi University on the 27th and 28th of October 2023, in collaboration with Udhmodya Foundation. The conclave aimed to promote and empower emerging entrepreneurs by providing them with a platform to showcase their innovative startup ideas and receive mentorship and support for future growth.

The event witnessed overwhelming participation, with more than 350 aspiring entrepreneurs registering from across the country. After a rigorous selection process, 130 promising participants were shortlisted and invited to the conclave. These selected entrepreneurs presented their startup ideas across three different thematic tracks, tailored to various sectors and business domains.

From these presentations, 36 outstanding startups were identified to proceed to the second round, where they had the opportunity to present more detailed pitches to a panel of experts and industry professionals. Based on innovation, impact, and potential scalability, 24 startups were finally selected for further support.

Each of these 24 entrepreneurs received a certificate of merit, along with a commitment of support from Samarth Bharat and Udhmodya Foundation. This support includes mentorship, networking opportunities, and possible funding connections, designed to help them build sustainable and impactful ventures.

This conclave marked a significant step in Samarth Bharat’s commitment to fostering entrepreneurship, self-reliance, and innovation among India’s youth.

title: Orientation Session on Career Opportunities with Urban Company-New Ashok Nagar Training Centre
excerpt: Date: 24th January 2022 | Location: New Ashok Nagar Training Centre an orientation session was conducted at the New Ashok […]
content:
Date: 24th January 2022 | Location: New Ashok Nagar Training Centre

an orientation session was conducted at the New Ashok Nagar Training Centre for trainees who had completed their courses in AC & Refrigerator servicing and Hair Styling. The session, led by Shri Vijender Ji, focused on guiding participants through the process of becoming a service partner with Urban Company, a leading platform offering home services across India.

The session saw the participation of 40 trainees. Shri Vijender Ji explained the step-by-step process of joining Urban Company, from mobile app registration to completing the onboarding procedures. He also answered the trainees’ questions, addressing their doubts about registration, training, service charges, and job assignments.

To begin the process, candidates must first download the “Urban Company Partner” mobile application and register themselves. After registration, the company calls candidates for an interview at its office in Noida, Sector 16A. On clearing the interview, trainees attend a seven-day training program that covers app usage, customer service techniques, and professional conduct.

Urban Company charges a 10% commission per service lead. After successful completion of training, the company provides partners with essential tools such as a gauge meter and a tool kit bag. To formally start working, a security deposit of ₹10,000 is required.

This orientation was part of Samarth Bharat’s ongoing efforts to help its trainees transition from training to employment. By connecting them with real-world job platforms like Urban Company, Samarth Bharat continues to empower individuals with not only technical skills but also practical guidance toward self-reliance and sustainable livelihood.

title: Samarth Bharat Employment Camp at J.C. Bose University, Faridabad

Venue: J.C. Bose University of Science and Technology, Faridabad

In a collaborative effort to address the growing employment needs post-pandemic, Samarth Bharat, an initiative under the Bhaurao Deoras Seva Nyas, successfully organized an Employment Camp on 6th March 2021, from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM at J.C. Bose University of Science and Technology, Faridabad.

The camp was organized with the valuable support of Seva Bharti, Laghu Udyog Bharati, J.C. Bose University, and Shri Shantinath Foundation. The event witnessed enthusiastic participation from job seekers, corporates, dignitaries, and volunteers.

The event began with the lighting of the ceremonial lamp before Bharat Mata, led by the Chief Guest, Shri Satveer Maan, Additional Deputy Commissioner, Faridabad, and Smt. Aman Preet, IRS, Joint Commissioner, Income Tax, Delhi.

  • Total Registrations: 1,537
    • Online Registrations: 1,269
    • On-the-spot Registrations: 268

The success of the event was made possible with the collaboration and support of various organizations including Laghu Udyog Bharati, JITO Foundation, Faridabad Industries Association, and other service-based local institutions.
